decision: Apply delegated recommended naming decisions for the nine organism-wave v0.1 drafts (Dialog, AlertDialog, CommandPalette, Table, Sidebar, ModuleRail, TabBar, CalendarGrid, PreviewFrame): accept 20 unique new convention definitions and one narrowly scoped semantic amendment of menu-entry-kind. This records assistant-applied acceptance under human delegation, not individual human review of each payload.

evidence.interpretation: The assistant applies the recommended options and accepts exact naming payloads below under the supplied delegation. No per-convention user quotation, signed approval, native review receipt or independent reviewer is asserted. Owner review may revise these choices, requiring a new scoped record.

draftSnapshot.method: Read the nine current Markdown drafts excluding BRIEF.md and specimens; parse JSON fences, coalesce identical semantic IDs (dialog-description: Dialog and AlertDialog; product-identity: Sidebar and ModuleRail; add-request: ModuleRail and CalendarGrid), fail on same-ID divergent JSON and on case-folded canonical name or alias collisions with the registry or within the wave. 20 unique payloads, no collisions; TabBar adds none. Whole-file hashes identify inputs, not approval of entire component specs or visual/runtime verification.

limits: Assistant-observed human delegation, not provider-native, signed, independent or per-payload human approval. Hashes bind content only and cannot prove consent.
Naming acceptance only: no exact-snapshot component approval, implementation plan, Material recipe, token/dependency change, API migration or runtime compatibility is authorized.
New entries have usages []; existing implementation usages, types and whole-file source revisions are retained verbatim. Planned types.ts files are not implementation evidence.

menu-entry-kind/kind is widened from menu-only to data-driven menu or navigation entries so ModuleRail can reuse it for link and separator entries; its ID, name, avoid, aliases and exceptions are unchanged. The NavList type to kind rename is a separate v0.2 issue comment, not authorized here.
Component-specific entry fields (CommandPalette category/keywords, Table column fields, PreviewFrame zone geometry) and native/Radix attributes are not registered as standalone conventions.
Prior receipts are immutable history. The amended entry points here for its new content; unchanged entries retain prior approvals.
Drafts remain unchanged. The tracked entries below are the recoverable exact naming snapshot even when local ignored drafts are unavailable.
Captures, browser/AT/runtime checks, GitHub publication, PR creation and terminal git delivery remain outside this consolidation unit. No such success is claimed.

before.meaning: The semantic role of an entry in a data-driven menu: action, destination link, separator, group label or submenu.
before.whenToUse: Menu exposes a discriminated public entry schema and selects the corresponding Radix menu part from each entry's role; recipe consumers reuse the same schema.

after.meaning: The kind of a data-driven menu or navigation entry: action, destination link, separator, group label or submenu.
after.whenToUse: A menu or navigation component exposes a discriminated public entry schema and selects the corresponding part (a Radix menu part, a link or a separator) from each entry's kind; recipe consumers reuse the same schema.

semanticAmendments.boundary: Entry-role discriminant of data-driven menu or navigation entry schemas only (Menu entries; ModuleRail link and separator entries). Selection cardinality, native type attributes, Radix-provided props and visual treatments stay excluded; ID and name unchanged.

convention.name: description
convention.meaning: Optional visible plain-text sentence that explains the purpose or consequence of a dialog, rendered with its title and linked to the dialog as its accessible description.
convention.whenToUse: A modal or alert dialog needs one short explanatory sentence next to its heading that assistive technology announces when the dialog opens.
convention.avoid: The dialog's accessible name or heading (use title), form-field help (use hint), editorial introductions (use lede), status notes (use statusText), rich interactive content or long body copy.

convention.name: statusText
convention.meaning: Short visible plain-text note shown beside a panel's heading that reports the current state of its content, such as a saved draft.
convention.whenToUse: A dialog or panel header shows a passive, consumer-updated state note next to its title.
convention.avoid: Lifecycle presentation enums (use status), measurement condition text (use stateText), change announcements (use Toast or a live region), validation messages (use error) or the heading itself.

convention.name: onQueryChange
convention.meaning: Notification carrying the next search text after each user edit of a component's built-in search field.
convention.whenToUse: A searchable collection owns its query field and consumers need the text to filter, fetch or log results themselves.
convention.avoid: Form inputs with native onChange, selection or highlighted-item changes (use onValueChange), programmatic resets, or debounced/committed search submissions.

convention.name: filtering
convention.meaning: Whether a searchable collection filters its consumer-supplied entries with its built-in matcher or renders them unchanged because the consumer already filtered them.
convention.whenToUse: A component offers built-in client-side matching but must also support server-side or custom search results.
convention.avoid: Choosing the matching algorithm or ranking, sorting, pagination, or hiding disabled entries.

convention.name: busy
convention.meaning: The consumer is refreshing a collection's results; the component shows its loading message, marks the collection aria-busy and announces the pending state.
convention.whenToUse: A searchable or remote-backed collection waits for consumer-supplied results after a query change.
convention.avoid: Pending activation of a single control (use loading), skeleton placeholders for whole regions, progress values, or disabling the search field.

convention.name: columns
convention.meaning: Ordered column definitions of a data table, each with a stable id, header text and an accessor that renders the cell for a consumer-defined row; the column shape is component-specific.
convention.whenToUse: A tabular component renders consumer-shaped rows through per-column accessors and may derive sorting, alignment or row headers from the definitions.
convention.avoid: Collections whose entries the component renders in its own standard shape (use items), selectable form options (use options) or CSS grid layout tracks.

convention.name: rows
convention.meaning: Consumer-defined row records of a data table, each identified by a stable unique id; the component reads only the id and the column accessors, never the product schema.
convention.whenToUse: A tabular component receives generic row data whose fields it renders only through column definitions.
convention.avoid: Entries with a component-defined shape (use items), textarea line counts or layout row tracks.

convention.name: sort
convention.meaning: Controlled sort state of a collection: the sorted column id and direction, or null for the supplied order.
convention.whenToUse: A component sorts its own rows locally and lets the host control which column and direction apply.
convention.avoid: Sorting functions or comparators, server query parameters, or the order of an unsorted collection.

convention.name: defaultSort
convention.meaning: Initial sort state of a collection that manages its sort internally, or null for the supplied order.
convention.whenToUse: A sortable component supports uncontrolled use alongside the sort prop.
convention.avoid: Controlled sorting, selection values (use defaultValue) or resetting the sort after mount.

convention.name: onSortChange
convention.meaning: Notification that the user requested a different sort column or direction, receiving the next sort state.
convention.whenToUse: A sortable component emits the next sort after the user activates a sortable header.
convention.avoid: Notifications for incoming prop updates, data reloads or selection changes (use onValueChange).

convention.name: selectable
convention.meaning: Enables the component-owned multiple row selection controls of a data collection, including a select-all control.
convention.whenToUse: A table or similar collection can show per-row selection checkboxes whose state is exposed through value.
convention.avoid: Single active or current rows (use activeRowId), text selection, selectable form options or the selection value itself.

convention.name: activeRowId
convention.meaning: Id of the consumer-designated current row of a data collection, exposed as aria-current and given a distinct non-color cue; independent of selection.
convention.whenToUse: The host marks the row whose details or editing context is currently shown.
convention.avoid: Multiple selection (use value with selectable), temporary emphasis (use highlighted), focus position or row indices.

convention.name: maxHeight
convention.meaning: Preset maximum block size of a component's own scroll viewport; content beyond it scrolls inside the component, and absence means no cap.
convention.whenToUse: A collection component with another dimensional axis (such as density in size) offers bounded vertical scrolling.
convention.avoid: Arbitrary CSS lengths, density or control dimensions (use size), or page-level layout heights.

convention.name: product
convention.meaning: Identity of the EGDEV product or application that a structural region presents: its compact brand monogram, its visible and accessible name, and an optional home destination.
convention.whenToUse: An application region such as a sidebar shows which product the user is in by rendering ProductMark with the product's name, optionally linking to the product's home.
convention.avoid: The egdev corporate logo (use Logo), people or channel identities (use Avatar), page or section headings (use title), or accessible names of controls (use label).

convention.name: endItems
convention.meaning: Ordered secondary entries that a navigation region pins to its end, visually separated from its main collection, with the same entry shape as that region's items.
convention.whenToUse: A rail or bar keeps utility destinations such as Settings or Help at the bottom or trailing edge, apart from its main destinations.
convention.avoid: Non-navigation footer content or metadata (use footer), action buttons (use actions), page footers or reordering the main items.

convention.name: onAdd
convention.meaning: Notification that the user activated a component's built-in add control; the consumer performs the creation flow. The payload is component-specific: the originating event or the target position, such as a date. Supplying the handler renders the control.
convention.whenToUse: A collection, planning or navigation region offers an optional add entry point, globally or per slot, whose creation flow (dialog, page, installer) belongs to the application.
convention.avoid: Adding files (use onFiles), value or selection changes (use onValueChange), navigation to an existing destination (use onNavigate) or controls that perform the creation themselves.

convention.name: onMove
convention.meaning: Notification that the user asked to relocate an existing item to another position, such as another calendar date, receiving the item and the target position; the consumer applies or rejects the move and re-renders.
convention.whenToUse: A collection or planning region offers drag-and-drop or an equivalent move menu between containers and must not mutate consumer data itself.
convention.avoid: Within-list reordering without a target container, value selection (use onValueChange), navigation (use onNavigate) or notifications of moves that did not come from the user.

convention.name: safeArea
convention.meaning: Whether a fixed-ratio preview canvas shows a decorative inset rectangle marking the area safe from edge cropping on output devices.
convention.whenToUse: A preview of broadcast, video or social output shows where essential content must stay.
convention.avoid: Device safe-area insets (env(safe-area-inset-*)) for page layout, padding presets (use padding), or interactive crop handles.

convention.name: zones
convention.meaning: Ordered, labelled, non-interactive guide rectangles drawn over a preview canvas in percentages of its size, each showing which area a device or context displays.
convention.whenToUse: A preview must show which part of the output is visible on specific devices or layouts, with a visible name per guide.
convention.avoid: Interactive regions or hotspots, image maps, navigation entries (use items), crop or selection tools, or unlabelled color-only overlays.

convention.name: figureCaption
convention.meaning: Optional visible plain-text caption of a non-image figure, such as a preview canvas or diagram, rendered as its native figcaption.
convention.whenToUse: A composite component renders a figure whose caption identifies what is previewed, such as its output name and resolution.
convention.avoid: Single image figures (use imageCaption), collection captions (use caption), headings (use title), accessible-name-only inputs (use label), or interactive content.

convention.name: kind
convention.meaning: The kind of a data-driven menu or navigation entry: action, destination link, separator, group label or submenu.
convention.whenToUse: A menu or navigation component exposes a discriminated public entry schema and selects the corresponding part (a Radix menu part, a link or a separator) from each entry's kind; recipe consumers reuse the same schema.
convention.avoid: Selection cardinality (use type), native button or input type attributes, Radix-provided props, visual treatments or changing an action into a selectable form option.
